title: Tangential drag destabilizes exact dust corotation in an ideal rotating magnetosphere
abstract: We test local stability of a charged point grain at exact rest in an ideal corotating stellar magnetosphere. The rotating-frame force vanishes only on the equatorial synchronous ring. A determinant proof shows that any positive tangential drag gives a positive real growth rate for every finite local magnetic-field strength and direction. An aligned-field cubic gives the rate. Tests on 1,000 general field and drag cases, 2,511 aligned cases and four full nonlinear dipole trajectories support the calculation. With a published stellar scale and charging and drag prescriptions, 1 micrometre grains at proton density 1e16 per cubic metre have local e-fold times of 5.8 to 6.2 days; 0.1 micrometre grains have times near 5,000 days. These are conditional model values, not measured lifetimes. The result adds a transverse stability test to dust trapping at field-line potential minima. It does not exclude long residence, finite-motion trapping, gas-supported clouds or dust supply, and does not explain the CPV population age trend. Original code, proof, model grids, validation and source hashes support reproduction without external data.

display.caption: Local growth times, four full dipole checks and conditional stellar scaling. Positive growth does not set a residence time without a source and displacement model.
